newsitem.title: USA: CSCE to raise margins on coffee futures May 29.
newsitem.headline: CSCE to raise margins on coffee futures May 29.

text.p: Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said on Wednesday it will raise the margin on the July 1997 coffee "C" contract to $10,000, including a $4,000 spot charge, effective May 29.
The exchange was unavailable for comment concerning the reasons for the change.
The margin September 1997 coffee "C" contract will increase to $8,000, including a $2,000 spot charge, the exchange said in a statement.
The previous margin for July 1997 was $8,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, while the September 1997 margin was $6,500, including a $1,500 spot charge.
The margins on all other coffee contracts will increase by $1,000 to $6,000, CSCE said.

In addition, straddle or arbitrage transactions require a minimum of $1,500 for customers who are CSCE members or members of the trade. However, the $4,000 spot charge for July 1997 and the $2,000 spot charge for September 1997 are applicable to all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving these months, the exchange said.
For customers who are not exchange members or a member of the trade, margins will be 140 percent above trade rates, CSCE said. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
